Various measurements of frequency values for a Wave object

Source: R/frequencyStats.R
frequencyStats.Rd

Calculates the peak, centre, bandwidth and quality factor. The quality factor (Q) is calculated at both -3dB and -10dB as discussed by Bennett-Clark (1999) <doi: 10.1080/09524622.1999.9753408>.

Usage

frequencyStats(
  wave,
  wave_spec = NULL,
  warn = TRUE,
  lowcut = 1000,
  plot = FALSE,
  output.unit = "kHz"
)

Arguments

wave

A Wave object. Stereo Wave and WaveMC objects are passed to allChannels(), which returns one set of statistics per channel.

wave_spec

A precomputed spectrum (optional, if not present will be generated), with its frequencies in kHz as seewave::meanspec() returns them.

warn

If TRUE provides warnings when values are not consistent

lowcut

Frequency below which values are ignored, in Hz, as every other frequency the package takes is. This argument was in kHz in earlier releases: the default is the same frequency as before, but a value given explicitly needs multiplying by a thousand.

plot

If TRUE plots the spectrum, with its frequency axis in output.unit, and marks the edges of the regions measured.

output.unit

Unit of the frequencies and bandwidths returned, "Hz" or "kHz". The default is "kHz", the unit they have always been returned in, and will become "Hz", the unit of every other frequency the package takes or returns, in a future release. A call that leaves it unset warns of this, once per session; one that sets it, to either unit, gets the same results before and after that change.

Value

A list with an entry for each of the -3dB and -10dB thresholds, and the spectral flatness of the spectrum. Each threshold holds the frequencies min, max, longest_min, longest_max, peak, centre, outer min and outer max and the bandwidths bandwidth and outer bandwidth, all in output.unit, and the quality factor Q. Q and the spectral flatness are ratios, the same in either unit.
